idiom_name: selector channel + field-vocabulary validation + boundary projection
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give the boundary one selector channel (query parameter, header, metadata entry or read mask field), parse it into dot-separated paths, and validate every path against the resource's canonical vocabulary before producing anything - an unmappable path is an INVALID_ARGUMENT, not an empty reply. Then project as close to the data as the stack allows: prune the query or DTO, trim the message, or filter the serializer output; only fall back to materialize-then-erase when the document already exists. Publish an explicit default (normally '*') so an absent selector keeps the historical shape, and keep permission filtering independent of the mask so a requested field can never widen access. Bound the selector - path count, nesting depth, which expensive fields are selectable - and version the field vocabulary additively.
code_sketch:
GET /users/42?fields=id,email,profile.avatar            # caller names the fields
# boundary:
select = parse(selector)                 # comma-separated dot-separated paths
validate(select, vocabulary(resource))   # unknown path -> 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT
reply  = project(resource, select)       # prune in the query, trim in the writer
# absent selector -> documented default view ('*' unless documented otherwise)
pitfalls: Ignoring unmappable paths instead of failing: the caller cannot distinguish a typo from a field that legitimately has no value, and the bug surfaces as 'the API returns too little'.
Leaving the default policy implicit, so the first refactor that turns on partial-by-default silently changes every existing caller's response shape.
Treating 'not requested' as 'not authorized' (or the reverse): authorization must run independently of the mask, otherwise a caller who names a restricted field is served it.
Letting the mask reach the data layer as raw text (SQL/JPQL built from caller input) turns a projection into an injection and exfiltration surface.

Wrong move: keying an intermediary cache only by URL while ignoring the normalized selector -> a full or differently projected response can be served to the wrong caller -> instead include the canonical selector in cache keys and Vary/ETag policy.

Wrong move: accepting arbitrarily deep, wide or recursive masks -> one request can trigger unbounded joins or resolver work and exhaust resources -> instead cap path count, depth and estimated cost before projection.

Wrong move: validating aliases and wildcards separately from query planning and serialization -> an allowed selector can produce a different shape or bypass a field policy -> instead compile one canonical field tree and reuse it for authorization, planning and output.
